summary:
NuGet writes the raw package archive SHA512 to the .nupkg.sha512 sidecar. Separately, PackageArchiveReader.GetContentHash uses the signed-content identity for signed archives and falls back to the raw hash for unsigned archives; PackageExtractor writes this value to .nupkg.metadata.contentHash. A signed archive can therefore legitimately have a sidecar value different from its lock/content identity. Comparing those two fields directly is a qualification-harness error, not proof that the package changed.

For controlled SDD build input custody, keep the joins separate: selected supplier whole-archive identity against actual retained bytes; raw SHA512 against the raw sidecar; genuine SDK-produced metadata contentHash against committed lock and asset values after actual locked restore; native SDK signature verification as its own required gate. Do not invent an unsigned-ZIP normalization or silently replace the selected raw archive with a payload-equivalent copy. Field agreement alone does not establish signature trust, resource-bearing compilation, installed-provider acceptance or publication. Preserve an original refused operation when repairing a wrong-domain harness check.

The cited immutable NuGet source defines these producer field semantics. It is not an assertion that a particular installed SDK was built from that revision, or permission to execute a tool, reuse mutable caches, weaken trust policy or reopen historical Unknown custody.
title: Keep raw NuGet archive identity separate from package content identity
